archetype: Golgari -1/-1-counter aristocrats: place counters, turn each placement into a body, turn bodies into drain, and hold three Mikaeus kill lines on top. strategic_frame.json declares `combo` and deck-audit adopts it, applying combo's overrides. The frame agrees with the deck: 8 tutors against combo's 4-8 and 5 protection against 4-6 both land inside the override bands.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts. It casts a 2-mana commander on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish games, hits the turn-3 land drop 90.2% of the time with zero unconditional taplands, and assembles commander-plus-a-payoff 67.2% of the time. What limits it is that every answer it owns points at a creature: across all 88 entries in cards.json, exactly two cards destroy anything (Crumbling Ashes, Mikaeus) and both destroy creatures, and nothing in the 99 destroys or exiles an artifact, an enchantment, or a land on the battlefield. One axis that reads as a problem is not: card-advantage's 8 misses The One Ring, Yawgmoth and Grim Backwoods. Ramp's 16 against 10-12 is a real overage of four copies. The one prescribed swap takes a single slot from it, Arcane Signet; a second ranked cut candidate, Dark Ritual, sits on the same axis and is not prescribed.

Toxic Deluge is not among them: -X/-X until end of turn is not a counter. I read all twelve. Exactly one does it repeatably, at will, for no mana, on a creature of your choice and without a cap: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, at the cost of 1 life and another creature. The other eleven are each gated. Serrated Arrows is free and at-will but capped at three activations, one per turn. Devoted Druid is free and repeatable but only on itself. Hapatra, Obelisk Spider and Necroskitter need combat damage. Blowfly Infestation and Host of the Hereafter chain off a creature dying — Host is why 'only Blowfly does this' is false, since it triggers on another creature you control dying and moves that creature's counters onto a target you control. Black Sun's Zenith, Fume Spitter and Grim Affliction are one-shot, and Contagion Clasp places one on entry and afterwards only proliferates for {4}. Stack 001 reached the same conclusion from the other direction: of the eight mana-free sacrifice outlets, one also places a -1/-1 counter, and that is the tutor target that matters.

cut_candidates.why: Pure acceleration in a deck 15 sources over the Burgess floor and 4 over the ramp band, and the worst rate among the pure-mana pieces. Eight of the 16 cards on the ramp axis do nothing but produce mana — Arcane Signet, Chrome Mox, Dark Ritual, Grim Monolith, Lotus Petal, Mana Vault, Mox Diamond, Sol Ring — and Arcane Signet is the only one of the eight that costs two or more and produces one mana per activation. The other eight are creature bodies (Birds of Paradise, Elvish Mystic, Llanowar Elves) or engine pieces (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Devoted Druid, Pitiless Plunderer, Deadly Dispute). The corpus is explicit about the trade: duplicated function goes before an uncovered class, and this deck has three uncovered classes.

It is the only card in the 99 with wither and the only one that takes a creature out of an opponent's graveyard, and the candidate pool's own note calls it 'arguably the most on-theme card in the archetype after Hapatra herself'. Cutting it removes the deck's only way to profit from an opponent's dying creatures and drops a body from 25 to 24. I am recommending it anyway, on its own terms: its wither fires only on its own combat damage from a 1-power body, and its reanimation needs an opponent's creature to both take a -1/-1 counter and die, while this deck aims its counters at its own creatures to make Snakes. open_questions.question: Does Ivy Lane Denizen loop in this deck, and does it convert? It is in the 99 and appears in seven of the nineteen two-card entries bracket_report.json lists: with Scurry Oak, and with six of the eight mana-free sacrifice outlets (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yahenni, Blasting Station).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ivy Lane Denizen is the load-bearing unverified card, not Scurry Oak. Those seven entries are exactly the seven of nineteen that route through none of Mikaeus, Blowfly Infestation or the commander, so a ruling on the Denizen settles this deck's only cluster of kills that survives Mikaeus being answered — and six of the seven pair it with a class that is eight deep, which would make the line redundant rather than a single point of failure. Mikaeus appears in 8 entries and Ivy Lane Denizen in 7; nothing else appears in more than 3. It is also one scenario rather than seven, since the six outlet records differ only in which free outlet is on the board. Note for whoever writes it: Ivy Lane Denizen triggers only when another green creature you control enters, and none of those six records names a card that puts a creature onto the battlefield repeatedly — that gap is the thing to resolve.

open_questions.question: Is Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation actually a two-card kill? goldfish_targets.json declares it as one and the audit measures it at 16.3% assembled (66.7% with tutors), but no stack has ever resolved it.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's second-most-measured target and its declared kill with the commander. Every number reported for it is a number about drawing two cards, not about winning.

open_questions.question: What is this deck's real rate of assembling ANY kill, rather than each named one separately?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The audit says outright that the schema cannot express the union of independent kills, and goldfish_targets.json declares no target at all for either non-Mikaeus route. So the simulator has never measured the deck's most redundant path to a win, and 2.5% and 16.3% both understate it by an unknown amount.

open_questions.question: Do the three Blowfly Infestation entries and the Hapatra + Host of the Hereafter entry survive a resolve-stack run, and what is the defensible two-card-infinite count?
open_questions.why_it_matters: bracket_report.json lists 19: 8 Mikaeus, 7 Ivy Lane Denizen, 3 Blowfly Infestation and Hapatra + Host of the Hereafter. Stack 001 refuted six of the eight Mikaeus entries and calls the figure inflated; open_questions[0] takes the seven Denizen entries. That leaves the three Blowfly entries (Nest of Scarabs, Flourishing Defenses, Hapatra) and the Host of the Hereafter entry, which nothing in the repo has ever examined. The floor of 4 does not depend on any of it — the 11 Game Changers force 4 by themselves — but a combo count nobody can defend is how a prescription gets sized against a number that is not there.

gaps: No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so nothing here is weighed against what strong Hapatra lists actually run. The single prescribed add comes from the deck's own colour-identity pool. A deck-recon pass would settle whether the format's answer to this hole is Assassin's Trophy or something the pool never surfaced.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so deck-audit cannot show it current. Its combo_count of 32 and its Mikaeus + Ashnod's Altar example are both contradicted by stack 001; treat the floor of 4 as resting on the Game Changer list alone.

Abstergo Entertainment exiles all graveyards, but it carries only land:fixing / land:untapped-dual / land:utility roles, and the breadth function reads oracle text only on cards holding an interactive role. The measured 1 therefore understates real coverage by one class — the deck's true position is 2 of 5, not 1 of 5, and the artifact, enchantment and land classes are genuinely empty. This is also why the prescription is one card and not two: Assassin's Trophy closes all three genuinely empty classes by itself, so after it the deck answers every class in Magic terms while the measure still reads 4.

Talon Gates of Madara phases out a creature on entry and Svogthos, the Restless Tomb is the one card in the 99 with no card_roles entry at all (roles coverage 98.9%). Neither changes a count here, but both are invisible to every role-driven axis.

Whether the interaction-breadth floor of 5 is the right target for a combo deck that wins from a board of dying creatures is a judgement the corpus does not make per-archetype; the target is the same one it sets for every deck.

Scope check: I could not diff against the iteration-2 document (it is not in git; HEAD is the iteration-1 commit and diagnosis.json has been overwritten in place), so I re-confirmed by phrase that the leaves I passed in iteration 2 are textually intact — open_questions[0]'s 'exactly the seven of nineteen that route through none of', axes[6]'s 'disqualifies seven of these same cards', cut_candidates[2]'s verbatim stack-001 scope disclaimer, axes[1]'s 'rituals and Treasure makers are one-shot', engine.components[6].count == 14, and marginal_note. No evidence of an unannounced tenth changed leaf.

The replacement argument is load-bearing and its central premise is false. 'Its reanimation needs an opponent's creature to both take a -1/-1 counter and die, while this deck aims its counters at its own creatures to make Snakes' — the deck aims its counters at OPPONENTS' creatures; that is its entire removal suite. deck-audit's interaction axis (14 cards) is nine -1/-1 counter placers aimed at target creatures: Black Sun's Zenith (X counters on EACH creature), Blowfly Infestation, Contagion Clasp, Crumbling Ashes, Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction, Hapatra herself, Obelisk Spider, Serrated Arrows, plus Yawgmoth. I read all 88 oracle texts in cards.json: the ONLY card that puts a -1/-1 counter on the deck's own creature as its function is Devoted Druid, which this same diagnosis (axes[6]) calls a self-paid cost that 'answers nothing'. Crumbling Ashes is the refutation in one card — 'At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy target creature with a -1/-1 counter on it' cannot fire without producing exactly the event Necroskitter is paid on, every upkeep. Black Sun's Zenith kills the whole opposing board with counters on it. And the premise's implied trade-off does not exist: Hapatra's trigger reads 'whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature', so killing an opposing creature with counters makes the Snake AND turns Necroskitter on. The document contradicts itself here — axes[11] and the verdict both say 'every answer it owns points at a creature', i.e. at an opposing creature, using these counters. Worse, the only mode in which the deck's counters do land on its own bodies is the Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation Snake chain, which open_questions[1] states 'no stack has ever resolved'. So a `painful` cut of the deck's only wither card and only opponent-graveyard reanimation is now justified on its own terms by an unverified line, against a verified and measured suite that says the opposite. The trade clause iteration 2 objected to was correctly removed; what replaced it is a worse defect, because it is a factual claim about the deck rather than a claim about the prescription. The entry's other two limbs stand (wither only on its own 1-power combat damage; dead against an empty board), and the hedge 'not a swap to apply blind' is real mitigation — but the sentence a pilot reads to decide is wrong.

Fetched strategy:deckbuilding.cutting via lookup-strategy --json. 'cut duplicated function before any uncovered class, and cut the ceiling card before the median one' is verbatim (it spans a line break in the section; whitespace-normalized it is an exact substring).
